name: Lincoln Red Imps FC
content:
Lincoln Red Imps FC is a football club from Gibraltar, founded in 1976 by Charles Polson and a group of players from local youth and lower-division sides. The club’s name is inspired by Lincoln City and the “Lincoln Imp” legend, and it quickly developed into a competitive senior team in Gibraltar football. After starting in the lower divisions, they earned rapid promotions and reached the top tier by the mid-1980s, where they immediately began winning domestic titles.

The club became the most dominant force in Gibraltar football, winning numerous league titles and setting a record streak of consecutive championships from the early 2000s to the mid-2010s. They also achieved multiple domestic doubles and trebles, solidifying their reputation as the country’s strongest side. Their long-term dominance made them a central figure in Gibraltar’s football development.

On the European stage, Lincoln Red Imps made history after Gibraltar joined UEFA in 2014, becoming the first club from the territory to compete in European competitions. They achieved landmark results, including progressing further than any previous Gibraltarian club and famously defeating Celtic 1–0 in Champions League qualifying in 2016. In 2021, they also became the first club from Gibraltar to reach a European group stage, continuing to break new ground for their country.

name: Prince of Wales FC
content:
Prince of Wales FC was one of the earliest civilian football clubs in Gibraltar, founded in 1892 during a period when football on the territory was dominated by British military teams. It played a key role in the development of organised football among the local civilian population and was among the founding forces behind early competitive structures on the Rock.

The club became one of the strongest sides in early Gibraltarian football. After the establishment of formal competitions, including the Gibraltar Football League in 1907, Prince of Wales quickly established itself as a dominant team. It won multiple league titles and was especially successful in the first half of the 20th century, collecting a total of 19 national championships and several cup victories.

Although the club remained highly successful for decades, its dominance gradually declined after the Second World War. Prince of Wales FC won its final major honours in the early 1950s and eventually dissolved in the mid-1950s. Despite its disappearance, it is still remembered as one of the most historically significant and successful clubs in Gibraltar’s football history.

name: Glacis United FC
content:
Glacis United FC is a football club from Gibraltar founded in 1965. It is one of the country’s most established teams and competes in the Gibraltar Football League. The club plays its home matches at the Victoria Stadium, which is shared by most teams in the territory.

During its early decades, Glacis United became one of the dominant forces in Gibraltarian football. From the late 1960s through the 1980s, the club won numerous league titles and domestic cups, establishing a strong winning tradition. At its peak, it was considered the leading club in Gibraltar football.

Over time, the club’s dominance declined, especially with the rise of other strong teams such as Lincoln Red Imps. Their last league title came in 1999–2000, but they have remained an important part of the national league. Today, Glacis United continues to compete in Gibraltar’s top division, focusing on rebuilding and developing new talent.

name: FC Britannia XI
content:
FC Britannia XI is a football club from Gibraltar, originally founded in 1907. It is one of the older clubs in the territory and has spent much of its history competing in Gibraltar’s domestic football system. The club plays its home matches at the Victoria Stadium, which is the main football venue in Gibraltar.

During the early and mid-20th century, Britannia was one of the dominant teams in Gibraltar football. Under its original name, Britannia FC, the club won multiple league titles, especially in the 1950s, when it was among the strongest sides in the country. This period established its reputation as a historically successful club.

After financial and organizational difficulties, the club was reformed in 2009 as FC Britannia XI. It returned to competitive football and even achieved promotion back to the top division in the 2010s. However, after further relegation struggles, the club eventually withdrew from senior league competition, though it remains part of Gibraltar’s football history and development.

name: Gibraltar United FC
content:
Gibraltar United FC was a football club from Gibraltar founded in 1943 during the Second World War. It was created by local players and quickly became part of the early development of organized civilian football on the territory. The club played its home matches at the Victoria Stadium and competed in Gibraltar’s domestic league system throughout its history.

In its early decades, Gibraltar United experienced strong success, winning multiple league titles and establishing itself as one of the dominant teams in Gibraltarian football. After a long period of competitive decline, the club briefly merged with Lions FC in 2011 before being re-established as an independent side in 2014. It then worked its way back into the top division through promotion from the second tier.

In later years, the club attracted attention for its modern ownership model and international partnerships, including involvement from well-known football figures. However, financial difficulties and instability eventually led to its collapse, and Gibraltar United ceased operations in 2019. Despite its end, the club remains part of Gibraltar’s football history as one of its more notable and eventful teams.

name: Europa FC
content:
Europa FC is a football club from Gibraltar, originally founded in 1925. The club has a long and complex history, including periods of activity, mergers, and rebranding. It is currently one of the established teams competing in the Gibraltar Football League and plays its home matches at the Victoria Stadium.

During its early history, Europa FC was one of the stronger sides in Gibraltar football, winning several league titles in the early 20th century. After a decline in performance, the club went through major changes, including a merger in the late 20th century and a later re-establishment as an independent team. It regained its identity and returned to top-flight competition in the 2010s.

In the modern era, Europa FC has re-emerged as one of the competitive clubs in Gibraltar. It has won multiple domestic trophies in recent years and also represented Gibraltar in European competitions after the country joined UEFA. The club continues to be a regular contender for league titles and cup success.

name: Manchester 62 FC
content:
Manchester 62 FC is a football club based in Gibraltar, founded in 1962. It originally started as Manchester United FC, created by local supporters who were inspired by the English club and were granted permission to use its name. The team has traditionally competed in Gibraltar’s domestic league and plays its home matches at the Victoria Stadium.

Throughout its history, the club went through several name changes due to sponsorship and administrative updates, eventually becoming Manchester 62 FC in 2013. During its early decades, it experienced periods of success in Gibraltar football, winning multiple league titles and domestic cups, particularly in the 1970s and 1980s when it was one of the stronger sides in the country.

In modern times, Manchester 62 has generally been a mid-to-lower table club in the Gibraltar Football League. While no longer a dominant force, it remains a long-standing and recognizable part of Gibraltar’s football system, continuing to compete at the national level and contribute to local player development.

name: Gibraltar FC
content:
Gibraltar Football Club was founded in 1893 and is regarded as one of the earliest civilian football teams in Gibraltar. It was established at a time when football on the territory was mainly played by British military personnel, and the club helped introduce the sport to the local civilian population. Its creation played a key role in the early development of organised football in Gibraltar.

The club became an important force in the first official competitions in the region. It was among the founding participants of early tournaments such as the Merchants Cup and the first organized league competition, which it won in 1895. Gibraltar Football Club also took part in early international friendly matches, including games against visiting Spanish sides, contributing to the growth of football beyond the local level.

In later years, the club’s success declined as other teams rose to prominence. Its last major league title came in the 1923–24 season. Eventually, the men’s team ceased operations, though the club’s legacy continued in different forms, with women’s football connected to the name still existing in more recent years. Despite its disappearance from senior men’s competitions, it remains an important part of Gibraltar’s football history.

name: St Joseph's FC
content:
St Joseph’s FC is a football club from Gibraltar, founded in 1912 and considered one of the oldest active clubs in the territory. It competes in Gibraltar’s domestic league system and plays its home matches at the Victoria Stadium. The club has long been part of the country’s football structure and is one of its most historically established teams.

Throughout its history, St Joseph’s has experienced mixed sporting success. Its most significant achievement came in the 1995–96 season, when it won the national league title for the first time. The club has been particularly successful in cup competitions, winning the Rock Cup multiple times and establishing itself as a strong contender in knockout tournaments.

In the modern era, St Joseph’s has remained a consistent top-division side, often finishing in competitive league positions and occasionally qualifying for European competitions. While it has not dominated the league in recent decades, it is still regarded as one of Gibraltar’s traditional “strong clubs,” known for stability, cup success, and long-standing presence in the domestic game.

name: FC Magpies
content:
Gibraltar F.C. is one of the earliest football clubs in Gibraltar, founded in November 1893. It was created during the early development of civilian football on the Rock, when the sport was mainly played by British military personnel. The club played a key role in helping establish organized football among the local population and was among the founding teams of early competitions in Gibraltar.

The club became historically significant by winning the first organized league competition in Gibraltar in 1895. It was also an early participant in the Merchants Cup, one of the first football tournaments in the territory. During this period, Gibraltar F.C. helped popularize football locally and even took part in early matches against visiting foreign teams, contributing to the sport’s growth beyond Gibraltar.

Over time, the club’s influence declined as new teams emerged and competition increased. While its men’s team eventually disappeared from senior football, its legacy remains important in the history of Gibraltar’s game. Gibraltar F.C. is still remembered as one of the pioneering clubs that helped establish football culture in the territory.
